why: Daniel's own currency edits (8 annotations): shekel amounts as digits with NIS after, "12,000 NIS".
behaviour: the speaker says one to three prices or amounts of money the way people say them aloud: shekels mostly ("two thousand two hundred shekels", "forty-two thousand shekels", "about three hundred shekels", "one fifty", "twelve and a half thousand"), sometimes dollars or euros ("forty bucks", "a hundred and twenty dollars"), occasionally "NIS" spoken as letters ("N I S")
rule: Write money as digits with thousands commas and the currency after for shekels: "2,200 NIS", "42,000 NIS", "about 300 NIS" (shekels, shekel, NIS, N I S all become NIS; "one fifty" in a price context -> "150 NIS"; "twelve and a half thousand" -> "12,500 NIS"). Dollars and euros take the symbol before: "$40", "$120", "€35" (bucks -> dollars). Keep decimals as said ("$4.50"). Never change the amount itself. Large amounts keep the scale word: "$2 million", "4.2 million NIS". A currency named without an amount stays a word ("some shekels", "the dollar"). Same convention as the ASR fine-tune's currency task (ASR-Training docs/dataset.md).
